title: Druxt 0.25.2; Drupal Canvas sites, no Drupal required
description: Druxt 0.25.2 renders Drupal Canvas pages in Fully Decoupled Nuxt sites, keeps signed-in responses out of the server cache, and makes v-model follow forms and filters. Run the demo in your browser, with no Drupal to install.

content.html: Drupal Canvas pages, rendered by Nuxt, and there's a site in this post you can start without installing a thing. Press Run and Druxt 0.25.2 boots in your browser, rendering the Canvas pages of a Drupal CMS site from a recording of its API, so there's no Drupal behind it.

Druxt is the Fully Decoupled Drupal framework for Nuxt 2, and Canvas is the page builder in Drupal CMS. 0.25.2 builds against it, and there's more than Canvas in it. Signed-in responses stay out of the server cache from the first request, v-model keeps up with forms and filters, and a failed resource tells you why. The upgrade is one command, plus two things to check.

content.title: Drupal CMS's Dashi site, rendered by Druxt 0.25.2 and Nuxt 2
content.caption: A Nuxt 2 site on druxt-site 0.15.2 and @druxt-contrib/canvas, reading the Dashi preset of Decoupled Drupal Mock. The source is on GitHub.

content.html: I wanted a demo you could run without setting up Drupal, so this one runs two things side by side. One is Decoupled Drupal Mock with its Dashi preset, which replays the JSON:API, Decoupled Router and menu responses of a Drupal CMS 2.2.9 site running Canvas 1.12.0. The other is Nuxt, and this is all the configuration it needs:

content.title: nuxt.config.js
content.highlighted: export default { modules: ['druxt-site', '@druxt-contrib/canvas'], druxt: { baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3005', proxy: { api: true }, }, }

content.alt: The demo's front page: Dashi's header with Home, Articles and Recipes links, the heading "Super easy vegetarian pasta bake", three linked recipe and article titles, and a band of four recipe cards with photos (Borscht with pork ribs, Fiery chili sauce, Crema catalana and Thai green curry). The footer reads "Served by decoupled-drupal-mock from a recording of Drupal CMS's Dashi site template. No Drupal is running."
content.caption: Dashi's front page, a Canvas page, as the demo renders it from the recording.

content.html: The front page and /canvas-external are Canvas pages, resolved by path with no Nuxt page behind them. Follow a link from the front page to a recipe or article and Druxt Entity renders the node in its default display.
Point baseUrl at your own Drupal and the same pages come from it. @druxt-contrib/canvas renders each Canvas component through a Vue wrapper you write, and the Druxt Canvas docs show how to name one.

druxt-schema 0.12.2 builds sites with Canvas installed. Druxt reads every entity view and form display while it builds, and Canvas 1.12.0 answers 500 when JSON:API asks for any page of them after the first, so Druxt now asks in smaller requests, filtered by entity type and bundle (#1022). 1.13.0 still has the bug, and it's reported against Canvas.

If you patched Canvas just to get the build through, the patch can stay or go. Keep it if one bundle has more than 50 view or form displays of its own, because that still stops the build without it. The demo's recording doesn't page its displays, so this is the one fix you'll only see on a live site.

0.25.0 added a server cache for the JSON:API index and menus, and it skips any request that carries credentials. 0.25.2 runs your request interceptors on a copy of each request before it looks in the cache, so a token your plugin adds turns the cache off from the first request (#1018). Before, the cache only saw that token once a response came back, and a response fetched for a signed-in visitor could be served to anonymous ones.
Register a plugin like this one under plugins in nuxt.config.js, and read the token from wherever your site keeps it:

content.title: plugins/druxt-token.js
content.highlighted: export default ({ $druxt, store }) => { $druxt.axios.interceptors.request.use((config) => { if (store.state.token) { config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${store.state.token}` } return config }) }

content.html: An interceptor that logs can skip that dry run by checking config[Symbol.for('druxt.processCache.probe')]. One that only knows the token after an await is still seen once the first response arrives, so put that token on the Axios defaults instead. @nuxtjs/auth-next already does, unless token.global is off. Menus follow the same rule, including an interceptor that only adds credentials to menu requests.

paragraphs.title: Signed-in responses stay out of the cache

content.html: v-model on the Druxt component now follows the module's value (#1005), so an entity form reports each edit to its parent:

content.title: pages/edit/_uuid.vue
content.highlighted: <template> <div> <Druxt v-model="entity" module="entity-form" :props-data="{ type: 'node--page', uuid }" /> <pre>{{ entity }}</pre> </div> </template> <script> export default { asyncData: ({ params }) => ({ uuid: params.uuid }), data: () => ({ entity: undefined }), } </script>

content.html: Getting that right took three more fixes. A value you set while the entity loads stays when the entity arrives (#1036). A field rendered in another component's slot reads its own entity's data (#1020). And v-model works on every module alongside druxt-entity, which is what lets an exposed Views filter apply (#1037). Change that filter on page three of a view and you're back on page one, as Drupal does it (#1032).
A failed druxt/getResource request carries its status code, so you can send a 401 to the login page and treat a 404 as missing (#1013). If the request never reaches Drupal at all, the status is 500.

content.title: Send a 401 to the login page
content.highlighted: async fetch() { const resource = await this.$store.dispatch('druxt/getResource', { type: 'node--page', id: this.id, }) if (resource.error?.statusCode === 401) { return this.$router.push('/user/login') } this.resource = resource },

content.html: JSON:API links now reach the browser as paths even when Drupal builds them on another scheme or host, such as https:// behind a proxy, so a client-side navigation stays on your frontend (#833). And DruxtSiteMixin imports in client-side code without pulling Node's fs into the bundle (#545). Thanks to Sebastix for reporting that one.
druxt-site brings the other six packages with it. Druxt now needs axios 0.35.0 or later, so its bundle holds one copy (#1029), and a site that pins 0.34.0 moves in the same command:

If your package.json lists another Druxt package of its own, such as druxt-schema, add it to that command too. An older copy at the top of node_modules is the one nuxt build loads, and an old druxt-schema still stops on Canvas.

Empty strings change too. The value of a module, a field or an exposed filter stays '', where Vue used to read it as true, and a custom field that emits '' passes it on to its parent. If your code checks for undefined to spot a cleared field, check for '' too.

Nuxt 2 is end of life, so 0.x is for the sites already running on it, and I want those solid before 1.0.0. A new site belongs on Druxt 2. Next is 0.26.0, due 8 December, the multilingual release and the last 0.x before the 1.0.0 release candidate. 1.0.0 is set for 2 February and Druxt 2 for 20 April, both on the milestones page.
So which Canvas components is your site built from, and which would you want rendered first?

content.description: Druxt is open source on GitHub. The demo's source is in Decipher/demo-druxt-canvas, ready to fork and point at your own Drupal site. Sponsorship is what keeps the 0.x line getting fixes like these while Druxt 2 is built.
